newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to raise VAT on luxury goods -- minister.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to raise VAT on luxury goods -- minister.

text.p: Turkish State Minister Gunes Taner, responsible for the economy in the new government, said on Thursday Turkey would raise value-added-tax on luxury goods and cut VAT on everyday goods.

"The VAT on luxury consumer goods will be raised slightly and in return for this the tax on goods such as foodstuffs, which are the daily requirement of our citizens, will be cut slightly," Taner said at meeting with union confederation leaders.

Taner said he expected international credit agencies to begin announcing in the coming days that Turkey's credibility had been restored with the establishment of the new right-left coalition two weeks ago.
The new minister said the economy inherited from the former Islamist-led coalition was a cause for concern.
"It is impossible not to be scared by the economic picture with which we are faced," he said.
He reiterated that the secularist coalition would refrain from intervention in interest rates and the foreign exchange market.
He also repeated a government target of $4 billion in privatisation revenues in 1997.
